1.stem: The passage implies that the survival of marine life through the glaciation is best regarded as evidence

options.A: that ice could not have extended to tropical latitudes at all.
options.B: that the tropical glacial deposits must have formed only after the freeze ended.
options.C: that photosynthesis proceeded unimpeded throughout the freeze.
options.D: against a fully frozen ocean and in favor of a belt of surviving open water.

2.stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the passage?

options.A: Orbital shifts, rather than carbon dioxide, account for both the onset and the eventual magnitude of the last deglaciation.
options.B: High-resolution dating of ice cores has become precise enough to distinguish events separated by only a few centuries.
options.C: Ice-core records demonstrate that changes in carbon dioxide concentration could not have influenced past global temperatures.
options.D: Although carbon dioxide did not initiate the last deglaciation, it was essential to the full magnitude of the resulting global warming.

3.stem: Which choice is best supported by the study described in the passage?

options.A: Late-departing birds arrived at their wintering sites much later than birds that left on time.
options.B: Birds that made frequent stops during migration arrived in worse condition than those that did not.
options.C: Departure timing had no measurable effect on the birds' winter survival.
options.D: Late-departing birds compensated for lost time in ways that left them weaker and less likely to survive.

4.stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support the researcher's claim?

options.A: Bond strength climbed to 31 MPa after 24 hours of curing and then fell back to a noticeably weaker bond by 48 hours.
options.B: Bond strength measured 22 MPa after 12 hours of curing, midway through the range the researcher tested.
options.C: Bond strength rose sharply from 12 to 31 MPa between 6 and 24 hours but changed little, to 32 MPa, by 48 hours.
options.D: The 6-hour trial produced the strongest bond of all, at 12 MPa, and every longer curing time gave a weaker result.

5.stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to support the botanist's claim?

options.A: Yield rose with each higher dose, from 18 kg with no fertilizer to 44 kg with the high dose.
options.B: The low-dose and medium-dose plots produced identical yields of 29 kg each.
options.C: The high-dose plot yielded less than every plot that received a smaller dose of fertilizer did.
options.D: The plot given no fertilizer yielded 18 kg, less than any of the three treated plots.

6.stem: Which finding would most strengthen the "old friends" refinement over the original hygiene hypothesis?

options.A: Children who suffer more infectious illnesses in their first years of life develop fewer allergies than their rarely sick peers.
options.B: Allergic and autoimmune disease is more common in wealthy countries than in poorer ones.
options.C: Children who bathe less often have fewer allergies than children scrubbed daily from infancy.
options.D: Farm-raised children with broad animal contact have fewer allergies than urban children despite similar rates of infection.

7.stem: Which choice best states an inference supported by the text?

options.A: The spider matches a new blossom the moment it settles on it, so switching flowers costs it no hunting time.
options.B: Yellow blossoms yield more prey than white ones, which is why the spider settles on them.
options.C: The spider's hunting success depends partly on how well its color currently matches its perch.
options.D: Camouflage matters less to ambush hunters than to web builders, since prey wanders close either way.

8.stem: Which statement is most strongly supported by the passage?

options.A: The early apparent abundance of hot Jupiters reflected the limitations of detection methods more than the true distribution of planets.
options.B: The radial-velocity and transit techniques are incapable of registering any planet smaller than a gas giant, however closely it orbits its star.
options.C: Hot Jupiters do not actually exist; the early surveys that reported them were registering artifacts produced by an immature detection method.
options.D: Improvements in detection sensitivity have revealed hot Jupiters to be even more common than astronomers once believed.

9.stem: Which choice best describes what the researchers infer about verbose patent descriptions?

options.A: They reflected the stricter legal standards that patent offices imposed on filings from regions with poor roads.
options.B: They indicated that inventions from regions with poor roads were more complex than those filed elsewhere.
options.C: Their thoroughness rose to offset inventors' limited ability to demonstrate devices in person.
options.D: They were written by inventors who distrusted their own physical prototypes.

10.stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support the chemist's claim?

options.A: As the temperature rose from 10 C to 70 C, solubility increased from 21 to 58 g per 100 mL.
options.B: Solubility fell steadily as the temperature rose from 10 C to 70 C, ending at 21 g per 100 mL.
options.C: At 10 C the salt dissolved to 21 g per 100 mL, the lowest value she recorded.
options.D: Solubility measured the same 39 g per 100 mL at both 30 C and 50 C.

11.stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

options.A: Beyond regulating craft, guilds provided their members with wide-ranging social and financial support.
options.B: Guild members paid dues mainly to secure the right to sell their goods in the town market.
options.C: Medieval Europe had no public institutions to aid families whose workshops were struck by fire or illness.
options.D: Medieval guilds existed chiefly to guard trade secrets and limit who could practice a craft.

12.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text with an inference?

options.A: Municipal composting facilities ought to raise their operating temperatures to match the industrial composters that can break the lining down.
options.B: The cups will decompose readily in any facility that accepts compostable material, since the lining breaks down over a standard cycle.
options.C: The manufacturer's compostability claim is misleading for the conditions most consumers can actually access.
options.D: Paper is fundamentally unsuitable as a material for beverage containers, since any cup made of it needs a lining that resists breaking down.

13.stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support the scientist's claim?

options.A: Of the 50 fields into which the predator was introduced, 41 showed only minor damage and just 9 showed damage that was severe.
options.B: Equal numbers of treated and untreated fields suffered severe damage, 9 in each of the two groups of 50 that the scientist compared.
options.C: Of the 50 fields with the predator introduced, 9 had severe damage, compared with 28 of the 50 fields without the predator.
options.D: More of the fields into which the predator was introduced suffered severe damage than of the fields left untreated, 28 against 9.

14.stem: Which choice is most strongly supported by the text?

options.A: Visible disorder bears no relationship at all to the level of serious crime in a neighborhood, since the two arise from entirely separate conditions.
options.B: Reducing visible disorder may fail to reduce crime when the community conditions underlying both are left unaddressed.
options.C: Removing visible signs of disorder such as graffiti and shattered glass is an effective way to prevent the serious crime that those signals invite.
options.D: Serious crime is what produces the visible disorder found in disadvantaged neighborhoods, reversing the direction of cause the original theory proposed.

15.stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to support the physicist's claim?

options.A: As insulation thickness increased from 1 to 6 cm, heat loss fell from 48 to 11 W.
options.B: The 2 cm sample and the 4 cm sample lost heat at exactly the same rate.
options.C: Heat loss increased steadily as insulation grew thicker, rising from 11 W at 1 cm to 48 W at 6 cm.
options.D: Heat loss with 1 cm of insulation was 48 W, the highest of the four thicknesses tested.

16.stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support the analyst's claim?

options.A: The East and South neighborhoods reported identical rates of regular physical activity despite their differing parkland.
options.B: The West neighborhood, with the most parkland per resident at 30 m2, had the highest physical-activity rate at 61%.
options.C: The North neighborhood had the least parkland per resident yet recorded the highest physical-activity rate of the four.
options.D: The West neighborhood had 30 m2 of parkland per resident, more than any other neighborhood in the comparison.

17.stem: The author of Text 2 would most likely argue that the reasoning in Text 1 fails because it

options.A: ignores how falling production costs can expand demand and create offsetting employment.
options.B: wrongly denies that any workers at all are displaced by automation, when even Text 2 grants that machines create losers.
options.C: assumes without argument that the historical pattern of offsetting hiring is certain to continue into the future.
options.D: assumes that machines will eventually match every human capability, leaving displaced workers no tasks to move into.

18.stem: Which finding, if true, would most strengthen the skeptical historian's argument?

options.A: Contemporary records document numerous vaults and towers that collapsed during or shortly after their construction.
options.B: Some master builders were paid considerably more than the masons who worked beneath them on site.
options.C: The surviving cathedrals display remarkably consistent geometric proportions across widely separated regions of Europe.
options.D: Modern engineers confirm that the surviving vaults are, by contemporary structural standards, remarkably efficient designs.

19.stem: How would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the argument in Text 1?

options.A: By agreeing that readers complete a text but denying that this makes every reading equally valid.
options.B: By arguing that readers play no legitimate role in interpretation.
options.C: By insisting that only the author's biographical intentions can determine a text's meaning.
options.D: By conceding that texts possess no stable meaning once they are published.

20.stem: Which choice is most strongly supported by the text?

options.A: Phlogiston theory was a baseless superstition, and its defeat by Lavoisier marked the triumph of experimental reason over uncritical tradition
options.B: Phlogiston theory was displaced because a rival accounted for the same phenomena while also resolving an anomaly phlogiston could not.
options.C: Phlogiston theory explained combustion, respiration, and calcination as well as Lavoisier's account did, and was displaced for reasons unrelated to evidence
options.D: Phlogiston's defenders were unaware that metals gain weight when they burn, an anomaly that came to light only after Lavoisier

21.stem: The passage is primarily concerned with

options.A: demonstrating that scientific literacy has no effect on public beliefs about any risk
options.B: identifying a condition under which a generally reliable relationship reverses
options.C: explaining why experts and the public disagree about the specific dangers of smoking
options.D: arguing that more information reliably narrows the gap between experts and the public

22.stem: The passage most strongly suggests that the first team's negative finding

options.A: cannot by itself settle the question, since decayed tissue may create a false absence of new neurons.
options.B: has been definitively traced to improperly preserved specimens.
options.C: proves that human neurogenesis stops after childhood.
options.D: is more trustworthy than the positive finding because it is less prone to false labeling.

23.stem: Which choice best states an inference that can be drawn from the text?

options.A: Seeding degraded reefs with Durusdinium-dominated stock would preserve the habitat that reef fish depend on.
options.B: A reef composed of surviving Durusdinium-dominated corals could fail to provide the structure that most reef fish require.
options.C: The principal threat to reef fish is the loss of heat-tolerant coral colonies during marine heatwaves.
options.D: Corals hosting common symbionts deposit calcium carbonate faster than any heat-tolerant species could.

24.stem: Which statement best captures the passage's view of gradualism's historical dominance?

options.A: It established that catastrophic events such as asteroid impacts and megafloods play no part in shaping the Earth's surface.
options.B: It reflected the fact that gradualism accounted for all of the available geological evidence better than any rival doctrine.
options.C: It was entirely a matter of professional ideology and had nothing at all to do with what the rock record actually showed.
options.D: It owed partly to gradualism's usefulness in disciplining a field prone to invoking miracles.
